title: Catch This Ruler: Your Reaction Time in Centimetres #brain #reactiontime
description:
Hold your thumb and finger open at the bottom of a ruler and have a friend drop it without warning. Pinch as fast as you can and read the mark between your fingers: that is your reaction time. A ruler falls from rest at a known rate (distance = g × t² / 2), so the centimetres turn into seconds: 5 cm ≈ 0.10 s, 20 cm ≈ 0.20 s, 30 cm ≈ 0.25 s. Many people catch it around 15 to 25 cm. The delay is mostly not your finger muscles: your eye has to see the drop, your brain has to process it and send the command, and the signal has to travel down to your hand. Because the ruler speeds up as it falls, every extra tenth of a second costs more ruler: wait 0.3 s and it has fallen about 44 cm, past the end of a 30 cm ruler. Try it three times and take the middle score; the dropper should wait a random moment so you cannot guess.
